intro: The Analects is a book of short sayings. Some are one sentence long. That makes them easy to quote and easy to misread. In this unit you slow down. You read famous passages from books 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 13 and 15 in James Legge's 1893 translation, word for word.

You will ask the questions close readers ask. Who is speaking, the Master or a disciple? Who is he speaking to? What English word did Legge choose, and what other words could fit? What do the nearby sayings add? How have Chinese, Korean, Japanese and Western readers taken the same line?

By the end you will be able to cite the Analects by book and chapter, explain key terms such as ren, li, xiao, de, shu and junzi, and write about a passage by describing what it says and how its readers have understood it.
bigQuestion: What does it take to read a short saying from the Analects carefully and fairly?

timeline.t: Traditional date of Confucius's birth in the state of Lu
Disciples and their students keep gathering his sayings (dates debated)
Versions of the Analects circulate in the early Han dynasty
He Yan's collected commentary on the Analects
Zhu Xi publishes the Four Books with his commentary
Joseon Korea makes Confucian learning central
The Analects is read in schools and homes around the world

words.d: the Analects' central virtue: goodness, humaneness; Legge writes "benevolence"
ritual and proper conduct; Legge writes "propriety"
filial piety; respect and care for parents and ancestors
virtue or moral power that draws others without force
reciprocity or considerateness; putting oneself in another's place
loyalty or doing one's best; paired with shu in 4.15
a person of noble character; Legge's "superior man"
"small person"; one whose mind turns first to gain
righteousness; what is right or fitting to do
Heaven; the high power early Chinese thought linked to order and fate
the teaching that words and titles should match reality
a book gathered from many pieces, often by several people over time

test.q: What does the citation Analects 15.23 mean?
test.why: The Analects is cited by book and chapter.

test.q: Which passage compares a virtuous ruler to the north polar star?
test.why: Analects 2.1 uses the pole star analogy.

test.q: Who speaks Analects 1.2 on filial piety as the root?
test.why: 1.2 is spoken by the disciple Yu Zi.

test.q: In 2.3, what do people led only by punishments lack?
test.why: They "try to avoid the punishment, but have no sense of shame."

test.q: What does Legge write for shu in 15.23?
What makes 15.23 a negative form of the Golden Rule?
choices: It says what not to do to others
test.why: "What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others" names what to avoid.

test.q: In 2.7, what distinguishes filial care from the support given to animals?
test.why: The Master asks what distinguishes support "without reverence."

test.q: What does the rectification of names in 13.3 ask for?
test.why: If names are not correct, language does not fit the truth of things.

test.q: Which disciple is praised in 6.9 for keeping his joy in poverty?
test.why: 6.9 praises Hui and his single bamboo dish of rice.

test.q: Which of these is a view scholars hold about how the Analects was made?
choices: Disciples and their students gathered it over generations
It was found in one tomb in 1973
test.why: Most scholars see it as a compilation made after Confucius's death.

test.q: In 2.4, what does the speaker say happened at fifty?
choices: He set his mind on learning
He knew the decrees of Heaven
He followed his heart without error
test.why: At fifty, "I knew the decrees of Heaven."

test.q: In 4.16, the junzi's mind is conversant with what?
What did Legge argue about the negative Golden Rule, a view many later scholars dispute?
choices: It was weaker than the positive form
test.why: Legge's notes called it weaker; many later scholars disagree.

test.q: Which pair appears in Analects 4.15 as the one thread?
test.why: Zeng Zi names zhong and shu.

test.q: Why do careful writers name their translation of the Analects?
choices: Word choices and numbering differ between editions
test.why: Translators choose different English words, and some chapter numbers differ.

write.prompt: What does the Analects say about how goodness spreads from a person to others? Cite two or three passages (for example 1.2, 2.1 and 15.23, in Legge's 1893 translation), explain what each says, and describe how at least two readers have understood them.
tips: Cite by book and chapter, and name Legge's 1893 edition.
Say who speaks each line: the Master or a disciple.
Attribute every idea: "the Analects says," "Zhu Xi read," "some critics argue."
Use the unit's terms, such as ren, xiao, de and shu, with a short gloss.
Compare readings; do not judge which is right.
